html:
A large early Maya city in the forest of the northern Petén in Guatemala, at its height in the Late Preclassic period, roughly 300 BCE to 150 CE. Its name means "the lookout" in Spanish.

El Mirador shows that the Maya built on a huge scale centuries before the Classic cities like Tikal. Its La Danta complex rises about 70 metres and is one of the largest pyramids in the world by volume. Raised stone causeways linked it to nearby towns across the swampy Mirador Basin, which has led some archaeologists to call it the capital of an early state. Lidar scans of the basin have since revealed many more buried platforms and roads.

The city declined around the 2nd century CE, perhaps after the land was overused. Power then moved to other centres, among them Calakmul and Tikal, which became the great rivals of the Classic period.
sum: A large early Maya city in the forest of the northern Petén in Guatemala, at its height in the Late Preclassic period, roughly 300 BCE to 150 CE. Its name means "the lookout" in Spanish.
